approach: Greedy sorting and sequential index tracking.
observation: Sorting the array allows smaller numbers to fulfill early index requirements (1, 2, 3...) as early as possible. Whenever a number is smaller than the required 1-based index, it cannot extend the current subarray and must start a new one at index 1.
bruteForce: Try all permutations and partitions of the array. Exponential time complexity O(N!).
optimalSolution: Sort array arr. Initialize count = 0, targetIndex = 1. Iterate through sorted arr: if arr[i] >= targetIndex, targetIndex++. Else, count++, targetIndex = 1, i-- (recheck current element as 1st element of new subarray). Return count + 1.
timeComplexity: O(N log N) for sorting plus O(N) for linear scan.
